hero.headline: Port St. Lucie City Council votes Monday on commercial rezoning near Tradition as neighbors voice concerns
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council is scheduled to vote Monday on a proposed land use change in Tradition that would convert nearly 9.5 acres near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive from residential to commercial designation. The request, submitted by Winding River Crosstown, LLC, would amend the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development plan by removing the property from residential designation and creating a new parcel designated for retail and office uses. The city says the change would allow for future commercial development on the site, but any future project would still need to go through additional review and approval processes. The proposal is scheduled for a second reading and final vote before city council Monday.

Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo, who live along the edge of the property, told WPTV two months ago they feared changing the land from residential to commercial could alter the character of the community they moved to call home. Joseph Mucciolo said the property is their backyard where they spend the majority of their day. He said it is going to be gone, and if they put up a wall it is going to look like a prison. Joseph Mucciolo said if these things come to pass, they may seek other grounds and other places to go. Margaret Mucciolo said they do not want over development.

The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the amendment with conditions in May. Those conditions include a 10-foot enhanced landscape buffer and architectural wall along portions of the property bordering residential areas, requirements to limit lighting impacts, and eliminating a possible future connection to SW Glenbrook Drive. The family says they worry losing the open space behind their home could impact the quality of life they value.

The Mucciolos say they want city leaders to consider their concerns before making a final decision. The concern for the family is not only what could be built but how it could change the feel of their neighborhood. The proposed rezoning represents one family's effort to have their voice heard as the community weighs commercial development against residential concerns in the master planned community of Tradition.

cards.headline: Florida Man Loses Home to Hurricane Milton Months After Paying Off Mortgage
cards.body:
A Florida homeowner who paid off his mortgage found himself facing catastrophic financial loss when Hurricane Milton tore the roof off his house just two months later. The homeowner had no insurance coverage at the time of the storm and was forced to pay for all repairs out of pocket.

The incident highlights the mounting pressures facing Florida homeowners as insurance costs have skyrocketed across the state. Many residents have been dropping coverage or going without insurance entirely as premiums have become unaffordable. The timing of the disaster proved particularly devastating for this homeowner, who had just achieved the milestone of full ownership before the hurricane struck.

Hurricane Milton caused extensive damage across Florida, with thousands of homes sustaining roof damage and other structural problems. The storm added to a growing list of natural disasters that have battered the state in recent years, driving up both insurance costs and the number of uninsured properties. Homeowners without insurance face the full burden of repair costs, which can run into tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars for major damage.

The situation reflects broader challenges in Florida's property insurance market, where companies have withdrawn from the state or dramatically increased rates following years of hurricane losses. State officials have been grappling with the crisis as more homeowners find themselves unable to afford coverage or forced to rely on the state-backed insurer of last resort. The case of this particular homeowner demonstrates the financial devastation that can result when disaster strikes an uninsured property, even for those who have worked to eliminate mortgage debt.

cards.headline: Martin County brush fires contained as Florida Forest Service warns more expected this summer
cards.body:
Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both fires are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said the county is in peak season for brush fires. The summer heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them receptive to ignition when lightning strikes occur. Rain often extinguishes these fires immediately, but sometimes they travel underground and surface days later.

The Florida Forest Service says the conditions that fuel these fires are not going away anytime soon. Grubitch explained that residents should not be alarmed but should remain vigilant during this peak season. He described the extreme summer heat that makes people not want to be outside, noting that this same heat is preparing dead vegetation to ignite easily when struck by lightning.

Grubitch said the public plays a crucial role in helping the Florida Forest Service do its job. He stressed that residents should never assume someone else has already called in a brush fire. If people see something, they should say something, as reporting fires quickly can make all the difference in how fast crews are able to get a fire under control.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner beats Alexander Zverev to win second consecutive Wimbledon title
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7), 7-6 (2), 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday for his second consecutive title at the All England Club.
cards.body:
Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7), 7-6 (2), 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday for his second consecutive title at the All England Club. Sinner's fifth Grand Slam title came in his first tournament since a second-round loss at the French Open in late May, when he wilted in a Paris heat wave. When Sinner ripped a forehand winner up the line on his first match point, the Italian dropped to the grass on his back in celebration.

Zverev appeared bothered by a knee issue following a slip to the grass on a key point in the third set. The match turned at 3-3 in the third set when Zverev earned his first break point after 2 hours and 42 minutes of play. Sinner produced a drop shot and Zverev slipped and appeared to hyper-extend his right knee as he attempted to change directions behind the baseline. Zverev grasped his knee in apparent discomfort and Sinner went around the net and helped his opponent up off the grass. Zverev quickly resumed playing but he appeared slightly hampered and slung his racket across the baseline in frustration when he missed a forehand and handed Sinner the first break of the match and a 5-3 lead in the third.

It was Sinner's 10th straight victory over Zverev, who was coming off his first Grand Slam title at the French Open. A year ago, Sinner beat Carlos Alcaraz in the final at the All England Club after wasting three match points against his rival in the Roland Garros final. Prince William joined his wife Kate and two of their children for the final in a star-studded Royal Box that also included actors Dustin Hoffman, Nicole Kidman and Ben Stiller.

Conditions were cooler in southwest London for the final, with clear skies and a temperature of 82 degrees Fahrenheit but it was also breezy, which led to a series of shanked shots from both players. Despite the defeat in the final, Zverev will leapfrog Alcaraz into the No. 2 spot in the rankings on Monday. Alcaraz missed both the French Open and Wimbledon this year due to a right wrist injury.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: TCCEED doubles employer participation in second year of paid summer internship program
cards.teaser: The Treasure Coast workforce development initiative placed 61 students in local jobs this summer as applications from area students tripled from the previous year.
cards.body:
TCCEED expanded its paid summer internship program in its second year, doubling employer participation across the Treasure Coast. The initiative placed 61 students in local jobs this summer.

Applications from Treasure Coast students tripled compared to the program's first year. The workforce development program connects local students with paid internship opportunities at businesses throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

hero.headline: Linda Noskova wins first Grand Slam title at Wimbledon after blowing five match points
hero.teaser: The 21-year-old Czech player recovered from a second-set collapse to defeat Karolina Muchova in an all-Czech final on Saturday.
hero.body:
Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. The 21-year-old became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth.

Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance, as was Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club. Navratilova looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with 105-step climb to panoramic views
hero.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, offers visitors a 105-step climb to panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
hero.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The red brick tower stands at the base of the Jupiter Inlet, where it has served as a beacon for mariners navigating the coastal waters. The lighthouse remains a working navigational aid while also welcoming visitors who want to experience its history and commanding views.

Reaching the top requires climbing 105 steps up a narrow spiral staircase, the same route lighthouse keepers once took night after night to maintain the powerful Fresnel lens that shone across the water. The climb follows the path of those early keepers who ensured the light remained operational for passing ships. The spiral staircase winds upward through the interior of the brick tower to the gallery at the top.

From the observation gallery, panoramic views stretch across multiple waterways and the ocean beyond. The Atlantic Ocean extends to the east, while below, the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet converge with the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers. Visitors can watch boats glide through the channel as sea breezes sweep across the observation area. The elevated vantage point provides a perspective of the coastal landscape that explains why this location proved ideal for a lighthouse.

The museum grounds include restored historic buildings that chronicle the lighthouse's journey from its construction before the Civil War through its years as an active Coast Guard station. These buildings offer details about the lighthouse's role in regional maritime history and the daily lives of those who kept it operating. The site preserves not just the tower itself but the supporting structures that made the lighthouse station function across more than a century and a half of service.
